extracted.intended_audience: crisis communication researchers, public relations scholars, and PR practitioners studying political messaging on social media
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic content analysis and coding of politicians' Twitter messages to identify crisis communication strategies (based on SCCT) and relate those strategies to audience engagement metrics during COVID-19. Includes inductive category formation and intercoder reliability procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCCT suggested strategies (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: SCCT’s suggested strategies include denial, diminish, rebuild, and bolstering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to match response strategies to crisis situations; they serve to reduce public blame attributions, improve perceptions of the organization, and alleviate negative emotions (Coombs references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny (SCCT general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deny indicates an organization’s deleted link to the crisis. The subcategories of the deny strategy are attacking the accuser, denying, and scapegoating (Coombs, 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied when actors attempt to shift responsibility away from themselves; look for discourse that shifts blame to other stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny - MEDIA
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = accusing media organizations of fake news, opposing reportage and stoking panic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code presence when the tweet explicitly accuses media of misreporting, lying, or creating panic (α = 1 in study table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny - DEMOCRATS/REPUBLICANS
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = criticizing Democrats in Trump’s case and Republicans in Cuomo’s case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when the tweet blames or attacks the opposing political party as responsible or culpable (α = 0.90).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny - FEDERAL
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = criticizing Trump, his administration and the federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when blame is shifted to federal actors or institutions (α = 0.73).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deny - EXCLUSION
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = projecting racial discriminations and xenophobia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when tweets employ racialized labels or rhetoric that scapegoats or excludes groups (α = 0.88).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diminish (SCCT and observed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Diminish strategy tries to minimize the perceived severity of the crisis and includes excuse and justification. Observed coding: 1 = diminishing the fatalness of the virus and the likelihood of contagion; describing the U.S. situation in a non-severe manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when messaging downplays severity, likens crisis to less serious events (e.g., 'like the flu'), or frames outcomes as non-severe (α = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuild (SCCT general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuild strategies serve to restore an organization’s tarnished image by providing both material and immaterial aid for the victims; subcategories include apology and compensation (Coombs, 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider as a possible strategy, but note authors excluded rebuild in their dataset because none of the tweets mentioned apology or compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolstering (SCCT general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bolstering is about drawing attention to positive attributes of an organization to protect its image, praising stakeholders, promoting better relationships with stakeholders while eliciting sympathy from the audience (Coombs, 2007).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code messages that highlight accomplishments, reassure audiences, or draw attention to positive aspects to improve public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolstering - GOVERNMENT
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = mentioning Trump/Cuomo’s achievements as leaders; mentioning the achievements of the government in Trump’s case or the local government in Cuomo’s case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when tweets explicitly list or praise governmental achievements or leadership successes (α = 0.91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolstering - ACTIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = ingratiating the proactive measures in handling the virus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when tweets emphasize specific actions taken or proactive steps as evidence of competent response (α = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolstering - EMOTIONALSUPPORT
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = conveying empathy; building intimacy; delivering encouragement, assurance and confidence; using emotional appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code for language of compassion, reassurance, and emotional connection with constituents (α = 0.91).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolstering - TRANSPARENCY
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = praising and promoting transparency in information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when the tweet highlights openness, data-sharing, or transparent communication practices (α = 0.90).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion (inductively identified new category)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new general category identified in the political context indicating an intention to promote cooperation, cohesion, and inclusion among various social members, institutions, and groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this category where messages emphasize collective action, cross-party cooperation, institutional coordination, patriotism, or inclusion; it is separate from SCCT’s original four strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion - PARTISANSHIP
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = creating party cooperation to tackle the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when tweets call for partisan collaboration or highlight cooperative efforts across party lines (α = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion - INSTITUTIONALCOOPERATION
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = promoting institutional cooperation, including cooperation with the federal government and different state governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code when tweets urge or describe institutional/ intergovernmental collaboration to address the crisis (α = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion - RALLY-ROUND-THE-FLAG
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = eliciting patriotism, societal cohesion and loyalty to the country/states to tackle the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code messages that invoke national unity, patriotism, or calls to collective solidarity (α = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion - INCLUSION
rubrics_metrics.description: 1 = criticizing those who discriminated minorities; promoting integration and cooperation among different ethnic and social groups; and enhancing benefits for vulnerable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code for explicit pro-inclusion rhetoric, defense of minorities, or advocacy for vulnerable populations (α = 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis type / crisis responsibility (SCCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis types provide a frame: victim crisis (public views organization as victim => less crisis responsibility), accidental crisis (outcomes considered unintentional), and preventable crisis (consequence of human error => highest crisis responsibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess perceived crisis responsibility to determine appropriate strategic responses; SCCT predicts stronger public attributions require more accommodative strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sticky crisis characteristics (COVID-19 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: COVID-19 is characterized as a 'sticky crisis'—complex, recurring, longitudinal—and enhanced by contextual factors such as misinformation, social issues, race and gender, and emotions; social/digital media integration increases complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that sticky crises may alter strategy effectiveness and produce new strategy forms (e.g., cohesion); account for longitudinal evolution of messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of analysis and coding design
rubrics_metrics.description: Unit of analysis: individual tweet. Coding approach: deductive + inductive; categories formed by pilot coding and grounded theory; variables coded dichotomously; categories not mutually exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform pilot coding, iterative category formation, and allow multiple strategy codes per tweet when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercoder reliability procedure and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Two researchers pre-coded 10% of sample (n = 48) and calculated Krippendorff’s alpha. After revisions, Krippendorff’s alpha ranged from .73–1 with an average of .94.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require intercoder reliability testing (Krippendorff's alpha); report α values for each code and aim for high average reliability; revise codebook when α is low.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manifest content categories (measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four categories captured as manifest content: account, date, retweet count, and favorite count (documented by data retrieval resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect these objective fields for each tweet to allow temporal analysis and engagement measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement metrics (operationalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Twitter engagement defined as the frequency of retweeting and liking elicited by COVID-19 related tweets. Engagement ratio calculated as means of interactions per tweet per 1000 followers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use retweet and favorite counts (and normalize by followers via engagement ratio) as behavioral indicators of audience response and to infer effectiveness of strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion criteria for dataset construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Three exclusion criteria were applied: (1) Unoriginal tweets, (2) Duplicated tweets, and (3) Tweets that did not show any crisis communication strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter dataset to original, unique, and strategy-bearing tweets to focus analysis on relevant messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic aims (research questions as evaluation foci)
rubrics_metrics.description: RQ1–RQ4: (RQ1) identify Trump’s and Cuomo’s crisis response strategies; (RQ2) examine how strategies co-occur; (RQ3) compare differences/similarities between the two politicians; (RQ4) analyze relationships between strategies and Twitter engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure analysis to (1) classify strategies in tweets, (2) explore co-occurrence patterns, (3) compare across actors, and (4) link strategies to engagement metrics statistically.
